title: GUIDE model — 2026
questions: When did GUIDE model tracks start in 2026?
What caregiver support does the GUIDE model provide?
summary: GUIDE tests coordinated dementia care and caregiver support. Established programs started July 1, 2024; new programs began services July 1, 2025 after preparation. Care navigation and round-the-clock support are model requirements. These facts describe model design; individual eligibility and payment still require the applicable specifications.

learning.limitations: Model guidance does not establish beneficiary eligibility, provider participation, actual contract terms, payment entitlement or causal benefit.

title: ACO REACH — 2026
questions: How do ACO REACH Professional and Global differ in 2026?
summary: ACO REACH runs through performance year 2026. Its Professional option shares half of savings and losses and offers primary care capitation. Global shares all savings and losses with primary or total care capitation. These headline shares alone do not specify final reconciliation, which also depends on model rules and participant circumstances.

learning.limitations: Model guidance does not establish beneficiary eligibility, provider participation, actual contract terms, payment entitlement or causal benefit.

title: TEAM model — 2026
questions: How long is the TEAM model episode in 2026?
summary: TEAM is a mandatory model for selected hospitals, covering five surgical episode categories from January 2026 through December 2030. Episodes include care through 30 days after hospital discharge. Risk-adjusted target prices cover included Medicare Part A and B services. The model does not make every hospital or surgical patient eligible.

learning.limitations: Model guidance does not establish beneficiary eligibility, provider participation, actual contract terms, payment entitlement or causal benefit.

title: ACCESS model — 2026
questions: When did the ACCESS model start in 2026?
summary: ACCESS tests technology-supported chronic care with payments tied to measurable patient outcomes. The ten-year model began July 5, 2026. Its model design is distinct from a per-service fee schedule; participation, covered conditions, outcome targets and actual payments require the detailed current model terms.

title: CBP — 2027 Star Ratings / MY2025
questions: What is CBP for 2027 Star Ratings?
What age range and threshold apply to CBP measurement year 2025?
summary: For 2027 Stars, C14 CBP uses 2025 HEDIS data, ages 18–85 and blood pressure below 140/90 mm Hg. Its weight is three. Eligibility and exclusions remain specification-dependent; Agere’s approximation does not produce a certified contract rating.

citations.title: CMS 2027 Part C & D Star Ratings Technical Notes

learning.limitations: Public specification knowledge only. Agere measure engines use simplified code sets and incomplete exclusions; they are not certified HEDIS calculations or CMS contract Star Ratings. CMS165 eCQM is a separate specification.

title: Diabetes adherence — 2027 Stars / MY2025
questions: What is the diabetes PDC threshold for 2027 Stars?
How many treatment days does diabetes adherence require for measurement year 2025?
summary: D08 diabetes adherence for 2027 Stars uses 2025 prescription events. PDC must reach 80%; the denominator requires two fills on different dates and at least 91 treatment days. No enrollment gaps are allowed during treatment. Agere’s simplified enrollment and drug mappings do not certify this measure.

citations.title: CMS 2027 Part C & D Star Ratings Technical Notes

learning.limitations: Public specification knowledge only. Agere measure engines use simplified code sets and incomplete exclusions; they are not certified HEDIS calculations or CMS contract Star Ratings. CMS165 eCQM is a separate specification.

title: Medicare Star Ratings — 2027 data periods
questions: Which measurement years feed 2027 Star Ratings?
summary: A Star Ratings year is not a universal measurement year. The 2027 edition uses 2025 data for CBP and diabetes adherence, while CAHPS survey collection runs March–May 2026. Contract scoring requires the relevant edition, measure-specific periods, weights and adjustments.

title: Population health — incidence and prevalence
questions: How do incidence and prevalence differ in population health?
Why must the population health numerator and denominator align?
summary: Population-health comparisons need defined cases, populations and time periods. Incidence concerns newly occurring cases; prevalence concerns existing cases. Numerator events should arise from the denominator population. Repeated measurements crossing a threshold must not be counted as repeated new cases without a defined incident-event rule.

facts.incidence_basis: New cases during a specified period
facts.prevalence_basis: Existing cases in the population at the stated time
facts.population_alignment: Numerator events arise from the denominator population

citations.title: CDC Field Epidemiology Manual: Describing Epidemiologic Data
citations.section: Counts and Rates; Measurements on a Continuous Scale

learning.limitations: These are methodological references, not a clinical risk score. Define case ascertainment, time, eligibility, missingness and observation coverage for each analysis.

title: PQI 90 Prevention Quality Overall Composite — AHRQ v2025
summary: AHRQ PQI 90 is an area-level composite expressed per 100,000 adults. It counts qualifying hospital discharges and uses the adult population of the geographic area as denominator, with component exclusions. A payer’s enrolled member-years are a different denominator and cannot silently be presented as the official area-level rate.

facts.denominator: Geographic area population age 18 and older

learning.limitations: Agere operational admission rates use observed enrollment and simplified codes. Report that adaptation; official geographic PQI requires the full specification and population denominator.

title: Population health — risk-adjusted comparison
questions: How should risk-adjusted population rates be compared?
Does risk stratification prove an intervention works?
summary: Observed and risk-adjusted rates answer different questions. AHRQ’s indirect standardization combines the observed-to-expected ratio with a reference-population rate. A valid comparison needs the specified model, population, covariates and version. Risk stratification for prioritizing review is a separate use and does not itself demonstrate treatment benefit.

facts.indirect_standardization: Observed rate / expected rate × reference-population rate

citations.title: AHRQ Quality Indicator Empirical Methods v2025
citations.section: Indicator rate definitions, pp.7–8; indirect standardization

learning.limitations: Do not label unadjusted rates risk-adjusted or infer causal intervention savings from a comparison. Existing risk engines require separate qualification.
